parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Determine the temperature of the gas.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: The average kinetic energy $E_{K}$ of a molecule of the gas is given by the expression $$E_{K} = \frac{3}{2}kT$$ where $k$ is the Boltzmann constant and $T$ is the thermodynamic temperature. The gas is heated at constant pressure so that its temperature rises by $125\text{ K}$.
parts.text: Use your answer in (a) to determine the new volume of the gas.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the increase in internal energy of the gas. Explain your working.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Use your answer in (b)(i) to determine the external work done during the expansion of the gas.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the total thermal energy required to heat the gas in (b).

stem: A cylinder contains $5.12\text{ mol}$ of an ideal gas at pressure of $5.60 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}$ and volume $3.80 \times 10^4\text{ cm}^3$.
